candidates.attacker_control: Content of a mustache template that the JStachio annotation processor compiles: an external template file referenced by @JStache(path=...)/@JStachePartial(path=...), an inline @JStache(template=...), or a partial. Anyone who can supply or modify a template resource that the victim build processes (shared/generated/CMS-provided template file, template supplied as 'data' rather than code) controls the identifier text that is copied into the generated renderer. Runtime model data alone does not reach the generator.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Literal template text IS escaped (OutsideMustacheTokenizerState splits out quotes/backslashes/newlines and CodeAppendable.stringConcat applies EscapeUtils.escapeJava), so this is an omission for identifiers, not an intentional 'raw template' feature. POJO member lookups use exact contentEquals (DeclaredTypeRenderingContext), so crafted names only resolve through Map/ContextNode-style contexts, which limits but does not remove reachability. The HTML escaper (& < > ") matches the mustache spec and its single-quote/attribute limitation is explicitly documented in Html javadoc, so it was not reported. No runtime model input reaches the generator. No tests are present in the snapshot and no build/test/scanner was run, so generated-output shape and exploit compilation were reasoned from source only.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary Java statements are compiled into the generated renderer, giving code execution in the application (and potentially in the build/CI environment during tests or later runs): confidentiality/integrity/availability compromise of the process that renders the template. Severity is bounded only by whoever can influence a compiled template resource.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The victim build runs the JStachio annotation processor and compiles a template whose identifier text is attacker-influenced. 2) The model must expose a lookup that accepts arbitrary key text so the crafted path segment resolves instead of failing with 'Field not found': a Map-typed member/root (MapRenderingContext.get) or a ContextNode (ContextNodeRenderingContext.find), e.g. the documented {{map.key}} usage. 3) The generated source is compiled (normal Maven/Gradle build) and the renderer is executed (application run or tests), where the injected statements run.
candidates.root_cause: The annotation processor emits parts of the generated renderer by string-concatenating template-derived text into Java literals/statements without escaping. JavaExpression.mapGet builds the lookup key as "\"" + key + "\"" (JavaExpression.java:98-102) and RenderingCodeGenerator.renderFormatCallJStache embeds the dotted path as "\"" + path + "\"" (RenderingCodeGenerator.java:148-161). These strings come from mustache identifiers/tag names, not from the code that has an escaping path: literal template text is neutralized by OutsideMustacheTokenizerState (SpecialChar/NewlineChar .javaEscaped()) plus CodeAppendable.stringConcat -> EscapeUtils.escapeJava. Names are not. MapRenderingContext.get (MapRenderingContext.java:59-77) and ContextNodeRenderingContext.find accept any key text, and IdentifierMustacheTokenizerState.character (lines 84-94) accepts any non-whitespace character inside {{...}}, so a crafted identifier can close the generated string literal (e.g., via a quote/backslash or a \uXXXX sequence that javac expands before lexing) and have the remainder of the tag compiled as Java code. The same unescaped-name pattern also appears in generated constants/comments (TemplateClassWriter.java:247 TEMPLATE_PATH, line 260 TEMPLATE_NAME, line 274 TEMPLATE_MEDIA_TYPE; TemplateCompiler.java print()/printCodeToWrite and section comments).
candidates.title: Template identifiers are interpolated unescaped into generated Java source (template-driven code injection)
candidates.trace: Template text -> BracesTokenizer/IdentifierMustacheTokenizerState.character accepts arbitrary non-whitespace chars in {{...}} -> TemplateCompiler._variable/_unescapedVariable -> TemplateCompilerContext._getChild -> MapRenderingContext.get(key) returns a Java expression for any key -> JavaExpression.mapGet concatenates the raw key into map.get("<key>") and RenderingCodeGenerator.renderFormatCallJStache concatenates the raw dotted path into a literal -> TemplateCompiler.print()/printCodeToWrite writes the string verbatim into the generated *Renderer.java (only literal text goes through EscapeUtils.escapeJava) -> javac compiles the injected text as part of the renderer, so the code executes whenever that template renders.
candidates.unverified: Not compiled or executed: I did not verify with javac that a specific crafted identifier compiles into a working renderer (the \uXXXX-before-lexing behavior and comment/statement completion are reasoned from JLS semantics), nor the exact per-context layout of the emitted line. I also could not confirm which upstream commit/fix (if any) this snapshot precedes, or whether the project treats template files as trusted input. Models without a Map/ContextNode context cannot resolve crafted names and would fail compilation, so exposure requires that pattern.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') (also CWE-95/CWE-116)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 444 repository files (371 Java, remainder XML/YAML/JSON/HTML/scripts); binary-like files are refused/skipped; no test directories exist in the snapshot. P1 relation index covers 439 files (5 source files missing from the index; unsupported analyses: control flow, data flow, semantic resolution, Spring runtime enforcement). I reviewed all modules at file level and deep-read: api/annotation (JStache, JStacheConfig/Path/Name/Flags/Interfaces/Lambda/Partials/Type), api/jstachio runtime (Escaper/Html/HtmlEscaper/PlainText/NoEscaper, Appender, Formatter/DefaultFormatter/SpecFormatter, Output/EncodedOutput/ByteBufferedOutputStream, Template/TemplateModel/TemplateInfo/TemplateConfig/Renderer/JStachio, spi/* including Templates/JStachioFilter/JStachioTemplateFinder/JStachioExtensions/JStachioFactory, ContextNode), compiler/apt (GenerateRendererProcessor, TemplateClassWriter, TemplateCompiler, CodeWriter, TextFileObject, ServicesFiles, tokenizer/token states, escape utilities, context/*, Interpolator, FormatterTypes), opt/jstachio-jmustache, opt/jstachio-spring*, opt examples, bin/, and spec/spec-generator. Coverage limitations: no build, tests, or scanners executed; generated prism classes and spec .mustache resources are absent from the snapshot; findings are static source evidence only.
limitations: No code was executed, compiled, or scanned; the code-injection lead is argued from source and JLS/javac semantics only and is not runtime-confirmed.
The snapshot has no tests, so intended behavior of the generator (especially identifier handling) could not be corroborated by tests.
5 files are missing from the P1 relation index and generated prism classes are absent, so a few referenced symbols were verified only indirectly via usage.
I could not compare against upstream/fixed code or advisories (no network access), so the mapping of this snapshot to a specific CVE/fix commit is unconfirmed; version is 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT.

The candidate's reachability depends on the model exposing a Map or ContextNode context; models without such a context would fail compilation for crafted identifiers, so not every JStachio template/model combination is affected.

rejected_leads.lead: Arbitrary file read/path traversal when loading templates: TextFileObject.openInputStream concatenates config.resourcesPath() with the @JStache/@JStachePartial path and calls Files.newInputStream without normalization or containment (compiler/apt/.../TextFileObject.java:62-128); the runtime JMustache analogue Loader.path does Path.of(sourcePath, templatePath) with no containment check (opt/jstachio-jmustache/.../Loader.java:53-77).
rejected_leads.reason: The path is an annotation value (same trust level as source code), the filesystem fallback is explicitly documented (JStache.RESOURCES_PATH_OPTION javadoc), and the existing single leading-slash stripping shows deliberate, if incomplete, path handling. Impact is build-time file read rather than a runtime boundary crossing, and no source evidence shows an intended check was omitted.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in bin/VersionHelper.updateTimestamp: DocumentBuilderFactory is used without disabling DTD/external entities while parsing pom.xml (bin/src/main/java/io/jstach/script/VersionHelper.java:464-489).
rejected_leads.reason: Build/release tooling parsing the repository's own pom.xml; no untrusted input path and low concrete impact. Hardening opportunity, not the strongest source-evidenced vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: HtmlEscaper does not escape the single quote/apostrophe (api/jstachio/.../escapers/HtmlEscaper.java:24-57), which would matter in single-quoted HTML attributes.
rejected_leads.reason: Matches the Mustache spec (spec test expects only & " < > escaped) and the limitation is explicitly documented in Html javadoc (element vs attribute escaping not differentiated, custom lambda recommended). No source evidence of deviating from intended behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: JMustache fallback extension is enabled by default when on the classpath and reloads templates from disk (opt/jstachio-jmustache, JMustacheRenderer.init/execute).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented behavior with explicit production-disable property and examples setting jstachio.jmustache.disable=true; template paths are derived from annotations, so no untrusted input controls the file read.

rejected_leads.lead: JavaUnicodeEscaper.toUtf16Escape indexes surrogatePair[1] and CodePointTranslator returns 1 consumed char for surrogate pairs (compiler/apt/.../escape/*).
rejected_leads.reason: Mirrors the Apache Commons Lang code this file is copied from; possible compile-time escaping subtlety but no attacker-controlled path established and it stays inside string literals.

summary: Reviewed the JStachio 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT tree (444 files: annotation/runtime APIs, annotation processor, prisms, JMustache and Spring integrations, bin/spec/doc tooling). Runtime rendering and escaping paths (HtmlEscaper, Escaper/Appender, Formatter, Templates, JStachioFilter, Output/EncodedOutput, Spring encoder/converter) look consistent with documented behavior. The strongest source-level issue is in the annotation processor's code generator: template-derived identifiers (dotted variable paths, Map/ContextNode lookup keys) are concatenated directly into generated Java source without the Java-string escaping the project already applies to literal template text (EscapeUtils.escapeJava / CodeAppendable.stringConcat). This creates a template-content-driven code-injection surface (CWE-94) into the generated renderer. Path-traversal file reads in TextFileObject/Loader and an unconfigured XML parser in bin/VersionHelper were considered but rejected as weaker (inputs are annotation/source or build-script data, and no evidence they violate documented intent). No build, tests, or scanners were executed; findings are source-evidence leads only.
